findings.description: AC5 violated: importing the registry imports Playwright. `from app.crawlers.base import BaseCrawler` runs at registry import time, and app/crawlers/base.py:10 does `from playwright.async_api import BrowserContext`. Verified: `python -c "import app.crawlers.registry"` leaves playwright in sys.modules (True). The module docstring (lines 6-7) claims the opposite ("imported lazily to keep Playwright out of import time"). This is also a regression for the crawl task: app/tasks/crawl_jobs.py now imports the registry at module level (line 7), so `import app.tasks.crawl_jobs` — pulled in by every Celery worker/beat process via celery_app's include list — now imports Playwright where the old `_CRAWLER_MAP` + in-function importlib did not. test_registry_import_is_lazy only asserts monster/naukri absence, so it passes while the Playwright clause of AC5 fails.
findings.fix: In registry.py add `from __future__ import annotations`, move the BaseCrawler import under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (typing.TYPE_CHECKING) so the annotations `type[BaseCrawler]` / `BaseCrawler` stay string-deferred, then extend the laziness test to assert no `playwright*` module is loaded (run that assertion in a subprocess, since playwright is already resident in the pytest process).

findings.description: test_registry_import_is_lazy pops every `app.crawlers.*` entry out of sys.modules and never restores it, so it permanently changes module identity for the rest of the session. Verified experimentally: after the pop, a re-imported MonsterCrawler is a different class object (`M1 is M2` -> False) and `isinstance(new_crawler, pre_pop_BaseCrawler)` -> False. It also drops app.crawlers.session_manager, whose module-level singletons (`_browser`, `_context_pool`, `_pool_lock`, app/crawlers/session_manager.py:20-24) would then be duplicated, while app.services.application_service (imported at collection via app.main) keeps the *old* `get_context`/`ApplicationReceipt`/`BaseCrawler` bindings. Nothing fails today (21 passed; full suite 257 passed) only because tests/unit sorts before tests/validation and the validation crawler tests import locally and assert self-consistently. Any later test that patches `app.crawlers.session_manager.get_context`, does a cross-module isinstance, or any run under a randomising/ordering plugin gets a silently ineffective patch or a false failure.
findings.fix: Do not mutate the shared sys.modules. Either snapshot and restore (`saved = {n: m for n, m in sys.modules.items() if n.startswith('app.crawlers.')}` ... `finally: sys.modules.update(saved)`), or — preferably, and this also enables CR-001's assertion — assert laziness in a clean subprocess via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', ...])`.

findings.description: `is_known_portal` is a pure forwarding wrapper around `registry.is_supported` with no added behaviour, in a module that already imports `is_supported` directly (line 7). Unlike `application_service._crawler_for_portal` (kept deliberately for the app/tasks/status_check.py:98 caller), it has no external caller — only line 160 and its own test. Fake abstraction per the structure lens.
findings.fix: Delete `is_known_portal` and call `is_supported(portal_name)` at crawl_jobs.py:160; drop test_is_known_portal_matches_the_registry (test_crawl_portal_accepts_every_registry_portal already covers the behaviour).

findings.description: The guard widened from case-sensitive to case-insensitive without normalising the value that flows downstream. Previously `crawl_portal('Naukri')` returned `{'error': 'Unknown portal: Naukri'}`; now the guard passes and the un-lowered name reaches `_run_crawl`, which uses it raw for `SystemPortalAccount.portal == portal_name` (line 49), `get_context(portal_name)` (line 60) and the `UPDATE ... WHERE portal = :p` at line 68. Result: an explicit error becomes a silent `{'status': 'skipped', 'reason': 'no_active_account'}` plus a stray browser-context key. Not reachable from today's callers (beat args and app/routers/admin/crawls.py:9 are lowercase), but crawl_portal is a Celery task invokable by name with arbitrary args.
findings.fix: Normalise once in `crawl_portal` right after the guard: `portal_name = portal_name.lower()` before `asyncio.run(_run_crawl(portal_name))`.

findings.description: A third hardcoded portal list survives the unification: `PORTALS = ['naukri', 'linkedin', 'glassdoor', 'indeed']`, used to gate `crawl_portal.delay(portal)` at line 20. The registry docstring now claims to be the 'single source of truth', but admin-triggered crawls still 400 on monster and shine — the same divergence class the story exists to remove (risk-map R4). Pre-existing and outside the diff's touched lines, so non-blocking, but it falsifies the diff's own claim and is a one-line fix.
findings.fix: Replace the literal list and the `portal not in PORTALS` check with `from app.crawlers.registry import is_supported, SUPPORTED_PORTALS` and `if not is_supported(portal):`.

findings.description: test_crawl_jobs_has_no_private_portal_map asserts on the absence of private implementation symbols (`_CRAWLER_MAP`, `_import_crawler`) rather than on public behaviour. It cannot fail for any correct implementation and pins the current internals against future refactors. test_crawl_portal_accepts_every_registry_portal already proves the crawl task and registry agree.
findings.fix: Delete the test; keep the registry-parity tests that assert behaviour.

findings.description: `patch.object(crawl_jobs.asyncio, 'run', ...)` patches the stdlib asyncio module object itself (crawl_jobs does a plain `import asyncio`), so `asyncio.run` is globally replaced for the duration of the with-block, and the test has to hand-close the orphaned coroutine (line 16). Harmless in the current single-threaded run, but it is a process-wide stdlib mutation to test a portal guard.
findings.fix: Patch the unit under test instead: `patch.object(crawl_jobs, '_run_crawl', new=AsyncMock(return_value={...}))`, leaving asyncio.run real.

findings.description: `getattr(importlib.import_module(module_path), class_name)` raises AttributeError (or ImportError) rather than the documented ValueError if a registry entry names a module/class that no longer exists — e.g. a crawler class rename. Callers such as app/tasks/status_check.py:100 catch broad `Exception`, so nothing breaks, but the docstring's 'ValueError if unknown' contract is only true for unknown portal names, not broken entries. No test exercises a malformed entry.
findings.fix: Optional: add a test that a bad `_REGISTRY` entry surfaces a clear error, or state in the docstring that registry entries are trusted.

findings.description: The story's problem statement names status checking of Monster/Shine as broken, and the caller is the reason `_crawler_for_portal`'s name was preserved, but no test covers the status_check path. It is covered transitively (status_check calls `_crawler_for_portal`, which AC1/AC2 tests cover) and the call site is unchanged, so this is coverage-completeness only.
findings.fix: Optional: add a test that the status_check portal grouping resolves a crawler for 'monster', or note the transitive coverage in the story.
